title: Dynamical locality and covariance: What makes a physical theory the same in all spacetimes?
exact_version: arXiv:1106.4785v3 (8 May 2012); read via ar5iv HTML rendering, version confirmed on the arXiv abstract page
locator: §1 final paragraph: conjecture sentence 'One might conjecture that a more detailed study of the category of spacetimes from this viewpoint would give a cohomology theory with many ramifications', followed by the pointer to Sanders [48]; §2.3 Props 2.4 and 2.6 (Cauchy-wedge and diamond connectedness); footnote 5 (nonconstant monotone ℕ-valued functions χ on the spacetime category used to build pathological theories); §6.2 remark that the twisting η is 'a cohomological issue'
assumptions: Loc = oriented, time-oriented GH spacetimes (finitely many components) with isometric embeddings of causally convex image preserving orientation and time-orientation; locally covariant theories as functors into a category Phys
conclusion: Loc splits into Cauchy-wedge-connected components labelled by oriented-diffeomorphism classes of Cauchy surfaces; the authors conjecture a cohomology theory of the spacetime category, realized by Sanders for Dirac-field freedoms; dynamically local theories satisfy the SPASs property
proof_status: established results per authors; this lane read and quoted only the listed passages, did not re-derive
open_questions: whether their conjectured cohomology theory extends to order/becoming structures — tested and answered negatively in this lane's RESULT.md
limits: sections outside §1-§3.2 and §6.2 not read; ar5iv rendering may contain conversion artifacts; the conjecture sentence sits in §1, with the technical wedge-connectedness in §2.3 (the task brief attributed it to §2.3)
relevance: primary source of the cohomology conjecture under test; also prior art for monotone functions on the spacetime category (footnote 5 χ)

title: The locally covariant Dirac field
locator: §3.4: cohomology of a category defined via the nerve (citing Roberts-Ruzzi [33] and Segal [38]); Theorem 3.15: 'The number of inequivalent Dirac structures whose locally covariant spinor bundles have four dimensional complex fibers equals the number of first Stiefel-Whitney classes of the category SSpac, i.e. the number of elements in H1(Z2)'; Remark 3.16: scalar/vector fields avoid the obstruction, general case expected to need nonabelian cohomology
assumptions: category SSpac of GH spin spacetimes; Dirac structures = locally covariant spinor bundles with adjoint, charge conjugation and gamma-matrix structure; equivalence via natural equivalences of the bundle functor
conclusion: freedoms in the Dirac construction are classified by H1 of the spin-spacetime category with Z2 coefficients (sign-twists along morphisms form 1-cocycles; compensating signs are coboundaries)
proof_status: authors' theorem; the reduction of the classification to cocycles/coboundaries was read, the full proof not re-derived
dependencies: Roberts-Ruzzi, Theory and Applications of Categories 16 (2006) 855-895; Segal, IHES Publ. Math. 34 (1968) 105-112
open_questions: nonabelian cohomology for more general freedoms (author's remark)
limits: the ar5iv text of the cochain definitions shows closed/exact labels apparently swapped relative to standard convention; the construction was paraphrased, not quoted; sections on Hadamard states and relative Cauchy evolution not read
relevance: nearest precedent for cohomology OF a spacetime category classifying construction freedoms; shows the H1 mechanism requires non-rigid targets, which is why it cannot transfer to germ clocks

title: Differential cohomology and locally covariant quantum field theory
authors: Christian Becker, Alexander Schenkel, Richard J. Szabo
exact_version: ar5iv rendering of the latest deposited arXiv version (header dated November 2016); arXiv version number not separately pinned
locator: abstract; §1 introduction and summary; §2.2-2.4 Cheeger-Simons differential characters and abstract differential cohomology; §3 Definition 3.1 (category Loc^m), Definition 3.3 (generalized Maxwell map), Theorem 3.9 (Cauchy morphisms act by isomorphisms on solution subgroups)
assumptions: Loc^m = finite-type oriented time-oriented GH Lorentzian m-manifolds with causally compatible open isometric embeddings; an abstract differential cohomology theory (contravariant functor on Man with the four natural transformations, BB14 axioms)
conclusion: generalized Maxwell maps as natural transformations on Loc^m; solution subfunctors with exact sequences; smooth Pontryagin duals with presymplectic structure; CCR quantization satisfies causality and time-slice axioms but violates locality, the violation tied to topological subfunctors (Pontryagin duals of singular cohomology groups)
proof_status: authors' theorems; spot-read only, not audited
dependencies: Cheeger-Simons 1985; BB14 axiomatics; BFV03; FV12; BDS14
open_questions: none taken up by this lane
limits: gauge/gerbe freedoms only; nothing on germs, precedence relations, or clocks; version number and page range not pinned from the journal site
relevance: the main later work on cohomology ON the spacetime category Loc; shows the FV programme was realized for Abelian field freedoms, not for order structures

title: Homotopy of posets, net-cohomology and superselection sectors in globally hyperbolic space-times

open_questions: whether its poset-homotopy techniques could compute anything for the germ preorder — judged not needed after the relabelling verdict
